subject: GMRFLib error no [20] when fitting a model with 1/0 variable

messages.author: 93f93e99d1eec3f2
messages.subject: GMRFLib error no [20] when fitting a model with 1/0 variable
parts:
Dear Help,

I have a problem with the inla() function. I first fit a model "response ~ 1+wtime+as.factor(seasgroups)+as.factor(delay)"
with
model <- inla(as.formula(theModel),data=dataGLM,family='nbinomial',E=E,control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE,link=link))
It works perfectly.

Then I change the theModel to include another variable that is composed of many 0 and a few 1 and no NA. It is included as f(,model='linear').
"response ~ 1+wtime+as.factor(seasgroups)+as.factor(delay)+f(outbreakOrNot,model='linear')"
When I do this INLA crashes with this error message:

" 
	GMRFLib version 3.0-0-snapshot, has recived error no [20]
	Reason    : Error occured in the GSL-Library
	Message   : GSL-library returned error-code [4]
	Function  : GMRFLib_init_density
	File      : density.c
	Line      : 680
	RCSId     : file: density.c  hgid: 7c663b7cdc57  date: Thu Dec 05 14:25:30 2013 +0100
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() : 
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does help; please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.

"

Verbose=TRUE has not provided me with more information.  I am quite puzzled. Do you have any clue what can cause such an error?

Thanks a lot for your help.

Best wishes

Maëlle Salmon.

> +as.factor(seasgroups)+as.factor(delay)+f(outbreakOrNot,model='linear')"
> When I do this INLA crashes with this error message:

I would guess that something goes to infinity here, and that less vague
priors for the fixed effects would resolve the problem. (also binomial
data is not always that informative...).

try with

f(..., model="linear", prec.linear = 1)

just to check...
